sources.entry: Clean-Me - Small macOS app that acts as a system cleaner (logs, cache, ...).

summary.one_liner: Clean Me is a small macOS app that scans and cleans system clutter such as caches, logs, the trash, Xcode derived data and mail attachments.
summary.what_it_does: The app has an analyse mode that reports how much space each topic (cache, logs, and similar) uses, and a clean mode that deletes the contents of the selected topics. Directories that need root are only scanned or cleaned if the user supplies the administrator password; otherwise those files are skipped and shown as 0 MB. A folder icon next to each topic opens the directory being cleaned so the user can inspect or remove items manually. Clean Me empties the contents of directories but leaves the directories themselves in place, so programs that rely on them keep working and permissions are unchanged. The README also says a full list of scanned directories is available. Removing iMessage attachments requires granting the app Full Disk Access.
use_cases: analyse disk space used by caches and logs on a mac
find out which directories take the most space on a mac
how_to_run: Install via Homebrew cask: brew install --cask clean-me
Or download the release from the GitHub repository, unzip it, and copy Clean me.app to the Applications folder
On first launch, right-click the app in Applications and choose open
Click analyse to see space used per topic
Select topics and click Clean to delete them
Optionally grant Full Disk Access in System Preferences > Security & Privacy > Privacy to remove iMessage attachments
stack: STPrivilegedTask (CocoaPods pod, used for root-privileged operations)
notable: Analyse mode shows space used per topic before anything is deleted
Only the contents of directories are removed, not the directories themselves
The password is stated not to be saved or stored in a variable
Installable through Homebrew cask or a manual release download
caveats: Some topics need the administrator password; without it those files are skipped
Removing iMessage attachments requires granting Full Disk Access, which the README warns against unless you trust the app
The author describes the cleaning feature as a side feature; the app was written mainly for analysis
